rationale.paradigm_idiomaticity: The code is relational in style: pattern-matching clause heads for chain/3, neg_pts/2 and consec/2, findall/member to generate pairwise sums, \+ and forall for universal checks, and a disjunction under once/1 for the collision tests. Weaker points: push_pt/3 uses a cut after a guard to emulate if-else; create_polygon/3 uses a cut-based dispatch on is_list; convex_hull/2 builds the hull with the clumsy append(A0,[_],A) idiom for dropping the last element; and the odd if-then-else/disjunction in seg_intersect/4 is hard to follow. A fully declarative version would use a cleaner formulation (e.g. last/2 or an explicit drop-last predicate).
rationale.language_idiomaticity: Uses standard library predicates well (maplist, findall, forall, sort/2 for dedup and ordering, append, reverse, length, is_list, once) and a sensible module export list. Naming is snake_case and arguments are documented in mode comments. Departures: polygon_data uses =.. to accept any compound, which is loose; velocity_data uses a cut; the first-clause cut in create_polygon is somewhat hacky; and the argument-order guessing in create_polygon is non-standard. reverse and append(A0,[_],A) could be replaced by library calls such as last/3 or append/2.
rationale.readability: Predicates are small and mostly named by what they do (orient, in_convex, edges_of, seg_intersect, on_seg, minkowski_hull). Comments explain the algorithms (monotone chain, configuration-space obstacle, mode docs). The convex_hull body with A, U, A0, U0, LS, RS is cryptic, and seg_intersect mixes an if-then-else with disjunction chains that needs careful reading. The dual-order create_polygon and polygon_data flexibility add some noise.
rationale.design: Decomposition is good: orient/4 is a shared geometry primitive reused for convexity checks, hull building, membership and segment intersection. minkowski_hull is reused by both public predicates, so the configuration-space approach is implemented once. Hull-of-pairwise-sums is simple and correct for convex inputs even if O(nm log). Weaknesses: the hull construction is duplicated across lower and upper chains instead of a single helper; the flexible input handling (polygon_data accepting arbitrary compounds, create_polygon swapping args) widens the interface unnecessarily; the degenerate-case handling of in_convex (needs 3 vertices) is partially patched by the edge-intersection fallback.

anti_patterns: cut after guard in push_pt/3 to emulate if-else
append(A0,[_],A) idiom to drop the last element instead of a helper
lenient argument-order guessing in create_polygon/3 using a cut
justification: The solution is largely declarative and well factored: orient/4 underpins convexity checks, monotone-chain hull, membership and segment intersection, and minkowski_hull/3 is shared by both public predicates. It uses library predicates (maplist, findall, forall, sort, once) properly. Minor blemishes are the cut-based push_pt/3, the clumsy drop-last via append in convex_hull/2, and the overly permissive input handling in create_polygon/3 and polygon_data/3.
